milestone: MFP Refund Ledger shipped: mfp-refund-ledger branch pushed (engine + letter gate + API, 29/29 tests) and synthetic demo deployed to hemangnagar.dev/rxguard-mfp/

interview.goal: Started as 'build something a new-age engineer would build' on the grocery project; pivoted to pharmacy market-gap research after judging margin analytics too crowded; landed on the Medicare MFP refund-reconciliation wedge and shipped a synthetic prototype + RxGuard module in one day. The goal changed twice, both times deliberately.
interview.slower_than_expected: Verifying the live deploy: the sandbox egress proxy blocks hemangnagar.dev, so a curl-based poll loop burned its whole 420s timeout reporting nothing while looking like 'still deploying'. Resolved by checking the GitHub Pages Actions run instead. Everything else (research fan-out, module build) came in at or under expectation.
interview.wrong_first: (1) One synthetic claim was force-coded 'overdue' although its own dates put it inside the refund window; caught pre-publish because the aging buckets ($6,510) disagreed with the KPI tile ($6,873). Fix: derive status from dates. (2) The evidence-table reference IDs overflowed the drawer; caught in the single design screenshot. (3) The /retro handoff brief assumed learned-behavior review emits JSON; it emits text (upstream learning.py:command_review).
interview.lb_candidates: None — learned-behavior had no hook events in this environment (fresh cloud container, hooks not installed). Degraded mode per SKILL.md; question answered from session evidence instead.

lessons.claim: RxGuard's demo page and Python engine must derive from one shared spec table (same curated fills, same FNV-1a hash) so both surfaces tell one story; never let them drift.
Every RxGuard surface that narrates money (the MFP escalation letter included) goes through the explain.py-style audit gate: any dollar amount absent from the fact pack is a hard rejection.

Before polling any external URL from a sandboxed agent, verify the egress proxy allows the domain; a blocked domain 403s forever and is indistinguishable from 'not ready yet' — verify deploys via the platform's own API instead (e.g. GitHub Pages Actions runs).
Before writing a parser against a third-party CLI, read its source or run it once to confirm the actual output format; do not trust a brief's claim about it.
evidence: learned-behavior learning.py:command_review (text, not JSON as brief assumed)

lessons.claim: On shallow git clones, address history by explicit sha, never HEAD~N — HEAD~N crosses the shallow boundary and errors.
evidence: retro@inputs.py diffstat bug, first guinea-pig run

lessons.claim: In curated synthetic datasets, derive every status field from its underlying dates/values instead of force-coding it, and reconcile aggregates to row sums before publishing — the $363 KPI/aging mismatch was the bug detector.
lessons.note: Held out of the playbook: it is the ancient single-source-of-truth principle wearing demo clothes; the SKILL.md bias check (>2 globals per retro is probably grandiose) fired and this was the weakest of three.
